sentences.text: Xiaosaurus was a small, plant-eating ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now the Sichuan Basin of China.
Its leg bone, the femur, measured exactly 11 centimeters in length.
The name translates to 'dawn lizard,' a reference to the ancient age of the fossils.
Scientists identified a unique straight upper arm bone that distinguishes this genus from all others.
Researchers uncovered two distinct individuals near Dashanpu in Sichuan between 1979 and 1980.
Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu formally named the type species Xiaosaurus dashanpensis in 1983.
The secondary specimen contains fragments including a dorsal vertebra, ribs, a finger bone, and two teeth.
The original authors placed the animal in both the Fabrosauridae and Hypsilophodontidae families.
Later analysis by Paul Barrett and colleagues in 2005 suggested the genus was provisionally valid.
Experts disagree on whether Xiaosaurus represents a valid species or is merely a name of uncertain meaning with unclear relationships to other groups.
